milestones.title: Phase 0 — Toolchain and Boot
milestones.description: Reproducible nxdk build, bootable XBE/XISO, platform compile profile, and observable engine startup.

milestones.title: Phase 1 — Platform and Memory
milestones.description: Core runtime services, QuakeC/game loop, input/audio, filesystem, and a controlled 64 MB memory envelope.

milestones.title: Phase 2 — NV2A Renderer
milestones.description: A dedicated RENDERPATH_XBOX capable of rendering the required world, models, materials, particles, and effects.

milestones.title: Phase 3 — Nexuiz Stress World
milestones.description: Legally clean converted content, deterministic flythrough, mixed workload zones, and benchmark telemetry.

milestones.title: Phase 4 — Validation and Release
milestones.description: Automated xemu execution, retail 64 MB soak testing, evidence, packaging, and documented limitations.

tracker.title: [Epic] Port DarkPlaces and a mixed Nexuiz stress world to the Original Xbox
tracker.objective: Track the staged work required to build, render, validate, and release the deterministic Original Xbox stress-world port.
tracker.summary: The acceptance target is a continuously looping, mixed-workload world running in xemu and on a standard 64 MB retail Xbox. Work is ordered by milestone gates; later-phase issues should not be treated as proof that earlier platform or renderer gates are complete.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Record the upstream baseline and fork maintenance policy
issues.objective: Freeze the source baseline used for the first Xbox bring-up and document how upstream DarkPlaces changes will be reviewed and imported.
issues.context: The fork currently tracks modern DarkPlaces at commit `5d80f03e26871b273da103f3b750820a3718c01a`. A long port cannot safely absorb upstream changes without an explicit policy because renderer and platform files will diverge early.
scope: Record the exact upstream repository, branch, and commit that starts the port.
Define whether Xbox work lands directly on `master` or through short-lived topic branches.
Define a review checklist for later upstream merges, especially `makefile*`, `vid*`, `gl_*`, `sys_*`, `thread_*`, and model/material code.
Create a machine-readable baseline file or documented tag name used by build evidence.
acceptance: The baseline commit is documented in the repository and visible in generated build/version output.
The update policy states which files require manual conflict review.
The policy prevents an automated upstream merge from silently replacing Xbox-specific behavior.
evidence: Link to the baseline commit or tag.
A sample upstream compare command and review checklist.
out_of_scope: Merging any upstream changes as part of this issue.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Pin nxdk and add a reproducible Xbox build entry point
issues.objective: Create the canonical build entry point for Original Xbox targets and pin every external build input needed to reproduce it.
issues.context: nxdk is the required open-source SDK. The desktop DarkPlaces makefiles assume host SDL/OpenGL libraries and cannot simply be invoked with a different compiler.
scope: Choose and record an nxdk commit rather than following its moving `master` branch.
Add an Xbox-specific makefile or wrapper that consumes `NXDK_DIR` and does not modify the nxdk checkout.
Define debug and release targets plus a clean target.
Generate XBE and XISO outputs in a dedicated ignored output directory.
Fail early with actionable messages when nxdk, clang/lld, or required host tools are missing.
Keep `make sdl-release` behavior unchanged.
acceptance: A clean clone plus the documented nxdk commit can invoke one command that enters the Xbox build.
The build prints the DarkPlaces and nxdk commit identifiers.
Desktop Linux CI still builds `darkplaces-sdl`.
Generated files do not pollute the source root.
evidence: Complete build log from a clean environment.
File hashes and paths for produced artifacts once the smoke executable exists.
Desktop CI result showing no regression.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Produce a bootable XBE/XISO smoke target
issues.objective: Build and boot the smallest nxdk executable owned by this repository before linking the DarkPlaces engine.
issues.context: A standalone smoke target isolates SDK, linker, XBE conversion, XISO generation, video initialization, and launch-path problems from DarkPlaces compile failures.
scope: Create a repository-local smoke executable using nxdk.
Initialize a display using a supported nxdk path and render a persistent diagnostic screen.
Print build identifier, detected RAM, launch path, and a monotonic counter.
Package the same binary as XBE and XISO.
Document launch commands for xemu and deployment to real hardware.
acceptance: The XBE boots in current xemu without external proprietary libraries.
The same XBE boots on a standard retail-memory Xbox.
The screen remains responsive for at least five minutes.
The XISO contains only redistributable project files.
evidence: xemu screenshot and complete console/serial log.
Real-hardware photo or capture plus launch method and console revision.
SHA-256 hashes for XBE and XISO.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Add DP_PLATFORM_XBOX and the initial feature-pruning profile
issues.objective: Give the Xbox port an explicit compile identity and remove unsupported optional subsystems from the first link.
issues.context: Using generic `WIN32` or pretending Xbox is another SDL desktop target will select DLL loading, desktop filesystem, windowing, and networking behavior that is inappropriate for nxdk.
scope: Define `DP_PLATFORM_XBOX` in the Xbox build and use narrowly scoped guards.
Create a documented first-link feature profile.
Disable dynamic library loading, video capture, browser/URL launch, clipboard, ODE, XMP, curl, crypto plugins, and other nonessential dynamic dependencies unless statically justified.
Select generic non-SSE code only where nxdk/target compiler compatibility requires it; do not globally remove safe x86 optimizations without evidence.
Emit compile-time errors for accidental incompatible combinations.
acceptance: The Xbox target compiles with a distinct platform macro and no desktop GL/SDL window dependency.
The first-link feature list is documented with keep/disable/defer reasons.
Desktop targets compile without `DP_PLATFORM_XBOX` behavior.
No proprietary XDK headers or libraries are introduced.
evidence: Link map or unresolved-symbol report demonstrating the reduced dependency set.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Bring up DarkPlaces core initialization without the production renderer
issues.objective: Link enough of DarkPlaces to execute `Sys_Main`, initialize memory/commands/VFS, and reach a controlled frame loop with a stub or diagnostic video backend.
issues.context: The first engine milestone should prove the core can run under nxdk before renderer complexity is introduced. It must fail visibly instead of hanging on unsupported host services.
scope: Add Xbox system entry and shutdown files rather than growing `sys_sdl.c` with unrelated branches.
Provide monotonic time, delay/yield, stdout/debug output, fatal error, and clean shutdown hooks.
Add a temporary diagnostic video implementation sufficient for engine startup.
Initialize command, cvar, memory, and filesystem layers.
Run a bounded idle frame loop and expose a controller-triggered clean exit/reboot path.
Guard every intentionally unavailable service with an explicit stub and diagnostic message.
acceptance: DarkPlaces reaches a named `XBOX_CORE_LOOP` marker in xemu.
The frame counter advances without unbounded allocation for ten minutes.
A deliberate fatal error produces a readable screen/log rather than a silent hang.
The same executable starts on retail 64 MB hardware.
evidence: Startup log from process entry through the first 300 frames.
Memory samples at startup, 1 minute, and 10 minutes.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Implement Xbox timing, logging, fatal-error, and crash diagnostics
issues.objective: Provide reliable observability before graphics and content increase the failure surface.
issues.context: Port work on xemu and real hardware needs the last completed stage, timing, memory state, and failure reason to survive long enough to be captured.
scope: Define a compact timestamped log format with build ID and sequence number.
Support on-screen ring-buffer output from early startup onward.
Write logs to a known writable path when storage is available.
Add named boot/frame checkpoints and a final shutdown marker.
Report fatal errors with source context when available.
Record high-water memory, current scene/workload marker, and last completed frame.
Document what can and cannot be captured after a GPU hang or kernel-level fault.
acceptance: Logs preserve ordering and remain readable after a deliberate engine fatal error.
A missing content file and an allocator failure produce distinct actionable reports.
The diagnostic path itself does not allocate recursively during out-of-memory handling.
Timestamp drift is characterized against xemu and real hardware.
evidence: Three fault-injection logs: missing file, deliberate assertion/fatal, and allocation failure.

issues.title: [Phase 0] Add host CI for desktop regression and Xbox cross-compile
issues.objective: Make every port change prove that desktop DarkPlaces still compiles and that the Xbox target does not regress at link time.
issues.context: GitHub-hosted runners cannot validate real NV2A behavior, but they can enforce source boundaries, pinned toolchain use, artifact generation, and basic static checks.
scope: Retain the Linux SDL release job.
Add an nxdk checkout at the pinned commit and compile the Xbox target.
Upload XBE/XISO, link map, build manifest, and symbols as workflow artifacts.
Run repository scripts that validate issue manifest, wiki links, forbidden binary/content files, and feature-profile consistency.
Use cache only for immutable toolchain/build inputs and never as the source of version identity.
acceptance: Both desktop and Xbox jobs run on pull requests.
A deliberate desktop compile break fails the desktop job.
A deliberate Xbox unresolved symbol fails the Xbox job.
Artifacts contain the build manifest and commit identifiers.
evidence: Documented local reproduction command matching CI.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Implement Xbox launch paths, VFS roots, and writable storage
issues.objective: Map DarkPlaces' virtual filesystem and generated-file behavior onto predictable Original Xbox paths.
issues.context: DarkPlaces expects a base directory, one or more game directories, PAK/PK3 search paths, and writable locations for config, logs, demos, screenshots, and benchmark results. Xbox launch locations can differ between XISO, HDD deployment, and dashboards.
scope: Define canonical read-only and writable roots for HDD and XISO launches.
Normalize drive prefixes, separators, case behavior, and path length limits.
Support loose files plus the archive formats required by the selected Nexuiz content.
Prevent writes into read-only media and redirect generated files to the writable root.
Create missing writable directories safely.
Add a startup filesystem report listing roots, mounts/search order, and free space.
Reject traversal outside approved roots.
acceptance: The engine loads a small test package from HDD and XISO layouts.
Config, log, demo, and result files are written to the documented writable location.
Missing/unwritable storage degrades to read-only operation with a visible diagnostic.
Path traversal and overlength tests fail safely.
evidence: Filesystem startup reports for xemu HDD, xemu XISO, and real-hardware HDD launch.
A file matrix showing read/write success and final physical paths.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Port threading and task queue with a verified single-thread fallback
issues.objective: Make DarkPlaces synchronization and task-queue behavior correct on the single-core Xbox CPU before deciding which asynchronous work is worth retaining.
issues.context: The engine has SDL/null thread implementations and a task queue. A mechanically translated threading layer can add contention or correctness risk without improving a single-core workload.
scope: Inventory every mutex, condition, thread, atomic, and task-queue dependency in the selected client build.
Implement required primitives using nxdk-supported facilities or a documented Xbox wrapper.
Provide a compile-time/runtime single-thread mode that preserves ordering.
Identify tasks that may overlap I/O or GPU submission and benchmark them before enabling worker threads.
Add shutdown, cancellation, and timeout behavior that cannot deadlock on fatal exit.
acceptance: Core and content-loading tests pass in forced single-thread mode.
Any enabled worker path produces identical deterministic benchmark state.
Repeated startup/shutdown does not leak thread handles or deadlock.
The default mode is justified by measured frame/latency data rather than desktop assumptions.
evidence: Single-thread versus worker timing comparison for every enabled worker.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Enforce the 64 MB memory budget and add allocator telemetry
issues.objective: Keep the entire executable, engine, renderer, content working set, audio, and safety reserve within a standard 64 MB console.
issues.context: The stress world is only useful if it runs on retail-memory hardware. Desktop-style caches and transient allocations can fail long after startup unless budgets and high-water marks are explicit.
scope: Measure executable/static/stack overhead before content.
Instrument DarkPlaces pools and major raw allocations by subsystem and lifetime.
Publish current, peak, allocation count, largest allocation, and failure reason.
Enforce configurable caps for world/collision, textures/lightmaps, models/particles, audio, renderer buffers, transients, and reserve.
Add deterministic low-memory fault injection.
Define purge/eviction order and rules forbidding per-frame heap churn in hot rendering paths.
Keep a minimum emergency reserve available to fatal-error diagnostics.
acceptance: The documented category caps sum to no more than 64 MB.
A full benchmark loop completes with at least the documented reserve remaining.
Ten consecutive loops do not show unbounded growth.
Fault injection produces a controlled report and preserves diagnostic output.
128 MB hardware is never required for acceptance.
evidence: CSV or log showing current/peak memory per category over a full loop.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Bring up QuakeC VM, client/server frame loop, and scripted entities
issues.objective: Run the minimum DarkPlaces game-code path required to drive a deterministic Nexuiz-derived world and animated workload entities.
issues.context: A renderer-only flythrough would discard much of the realistic CPU and state-management workload. The benchmark should retain QuakeC execution, entity updates, and the normal client/server frame sequence where practical.
scope: Load a legally redistributable minimal QuakeC test program through the Xbox VFS.
Initialize server VM, client VM/CSQC only where required, strings, edicts, and builtins.
Run fixed-step scripted entities and a camera trigger in a small test map.
Disable network discovery/master-server behavior for benchmark mode.
Identify unsupported builtins and classify each as implement, stub-with-error, or not required.
Add deterministic seed and fixed initialization ordering.
acceptance: A scripted entity moves identically across repeated xemu runs.
The VM executes for 30 minutes without string/edict growth outside defined bounds.
Unsupported builtins fail with their name and call context.
Benchmark mode makes no outbound network attempt.
evidence: Per-frame state hash for at least three repeated runs.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Validate collision, movement, animation timing, and deterministic simulation
issues.objective: Ensure the world update path used by the camera and stress entities is stable and repeatable before visual output is judged.
issues.context: Timing and floating-point differences can cause a recorded path or scripted workload to diverge, invalidating comparisons between xemu branches and real hardware.
scope: Choose the benchmark simulation tick policy and document render interpolation.
Validate BSP collision traces, entity linking, movement, and trigger order in a headless test scene.
Set and record all random seeds affecting particles, entities, and camera events.
Generate periodic compact state hashes from camera/entity positions and important workload counters.
Define tolerance rules for values that cannot be bit-identical.
Detect time discontinuities and prevent catch-up spirals from changing workload composition.
acceptance: Three clean runs produce matching state hashes at every checkpoint or remain within documented tolerances.
A deliberately delayed frame does not permanently desynchronize scripted events.
xemu and hardware complete the same sequence of workload markers.
evidence: State-hash logs for repeated xemu runs and one hardware run.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Port Xbox controller input and benchmark operator controls
issues.objective: Support normal menu/console interaction plus a minimal set of controls for unattended and manual benchmark operation.
issues.context: nxdk includes controller support, but `vid_sdl.c` combines desktop window/input and GL responsibilities. Xbox input should be isolated instead of retaining irrelevant window behavior.
scope: Map Xbox controller axes, triggers, buttons, and hot-plug state into DarkPlaces key/joystick events.
Implement calibrated deadzones and stable axis normalization.
Provide benchmark controls for start/pause/resume, restart loop, skip to workload marker, toggle overlay, write result snapshot, and clean exit/reboot.
Prevent accidental input from altering an unattended deterministic run.
Expose controller detection and raw-state diagnostics.
acceptance: All controls work in menus/console and benchmark mode.
Disconnect/reconnect does not crash or leave a stuck input state.
Unattended mode ignores gameplay movement input while retaining the documented emergency controls.
Raw values and final mapped values are visible in diagnostic mode.
evidence: Video or event log demonstrating benchmark controls.

issues.title: [Phase 1] Port audio output and preserve a deterministic no-audio mode
issues.objective: Provide representative audio workload without making audio a blocker for early graphics bring-up.
issues.context: The final stress world benefits from mixed CPU/I/O load, but renderer development must remain possible with sound disabled and without hidden mixer drift affecting determinism.
scope: Implement or adapt a supported nxdk audio backend for DarkPlaces' mixed PCM output.
Define sample format, channel count, buffer size, and underrun reporting.
Load and play the minimum selected WAV/OGG content only if the decoder fits the dependency and memory policy.
Retain `snd_null` as a tested command-line/config mode.
Measure mixer memory and CPU cost.
Keep audio timing from becoming the benchmark simulation clock.
acceptance: Representative positional and ambient sounds play without sustained underruns.
No-audio mode completes the same state-hash sequence.
Audio buffers stay within the assigned memory cap.
Audio failure falls back or aborts according to a documented policy.
evidence: Underrun count and audio CPU/memory statistics for a full loop.
State-hash comparison with audio enabled and disabled.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Approve the RENDERPATH_XBOX NV2A renderer decision record
issues.objective: Lock the renderer architecture, supported feature tiers, and translation boundary before large graphics changes begin.
issues.context: Modern DarkPlaces exposes only GL 3.2 and GLES2 render paths, both centered on GLSL permutations. nxdk exposes pbkit/NV2A facilities and shader assembly tools, not a compatible GL implementation.
scope: Document why a native `RENDERPATH_XBOX` is preferred over porting a desktop GL stack or forcing GLES2.
Define the boundary between existing DarkPlaces scene/material preparation and Xbox command submission.
Define the initial supported surface/model/2D feature set.
Classify every required effect as native, multipass, approximate, disabled, or deferred.
Define shader/combiner recipe ownership and how unsupported permutations fail.
Define batching, transient buffer, synchronization, and frame-present policies.
Record expected xemu-versus-hardware validation points.
acceptance: The decision record maps directly to `vid.h`, `gl_backend.c`, `gl_rmain.c`, `gl_rsurf.c`, `gl_textures.c`, and the planned Xbox files.
There is no claim that nxdk SDL2 supplies the 3D backend.
The document names the first visible rendering milestone and all deliberate exclusions.
Any alternative architecture is either rejected with reasons or moved to a separate experiment.
evidence: Reviewed decision document committed to the wiki.
A renderer call-flow diagram from world submission to NV2A present.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Add the backend seam and compile RENDERPATH_XBOX
issues.objective: Introduce the Xbox render path without scattering NV2A calls through world/model code.
issues.context: DarkPlaces' current `gl_*` files mix abstract mesh/state operations with GL-specific objects and shader selection. The port needs a narrow transition layer that can be compiled and tested before it renders a complete scene.
scope: Add `RENDERPATH_XBOX` and Xbox capability fields with conservative limits.
Create Xbox video/render source files and a build object list.
Route frame begin/end, viewport, clear, blend/depth/cull state, textures, buffers, and draw calls through explicit backend entry points.
Use compile-time assertions or unsupported-operation diagnostics instead of silently falling through GL cases.
Keep GL32/GLES2 code paths source-compatible and behaviorally unchanged.
Add a diagnostic command that prints Xbox renderer caps and disabled features.
acceptance: The Xbox client links with `RENDERPATH_XBOX` selected and no OpenGL library.
Desktop GL32/GLES2 builds pass CI.
Unsupported render operations identify their caller/category once without per-frame log spam.
The Xbox renderer can clear and present a frame through the DarkPlaces frame lifecycle.
evidence: Link map proving no OpenGL dependency.
xemu clear/present capture and renderer-capability log.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Implement NV2A device, framebuffer, pushbuffer, and present lifecycle
issues.objective: Create a robust frame lifecycle suitable for long unattended stress loops.
issues.context: The renderer needs explicit ownership of display mode, color/depth buffers, pushbuffer space, GPU synchronization, and recovery diagnostics. A single successful triangle is not enough for a soak workload.
scope: Select baseline video modes and a single acceptance mode, initially 640x480 unless evidence changes it.
Initialize pbkit/NV2A state and allocate color/depth buffers within the renderer budget.
Implement begin frame, clear, viewport/scissor, submit, wait/fence policy, and present.
Track pushbuffer usage, waits, wraps, and high-water marks.
Add a GPU progress marker or best available hang diagnostic.
Ensure clean shutdown/restart does not leave stale GPU state.
Document vblank/vsync policy for benchmark and uncapped diagnostic modes.
acceptance: A DarkPlaces-owned color/depth test runs for 60 minutes without pushbuffer exhaustion or allocation growth.
Frame presentation works in xemu and on real hardware.
Resolution, pitch, depth format, and buffer memory are reported.
A deliberate oversized submission is rejected or split without corrupting later frames.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Implement mesh buffers, vertex formats, state caching, and draw submission
issues.objective: Translate DarkPlaces mesh batches into bounded NV2A vertex/index submissions with low CPU overhead.
issues.context: The mixed world will stress both large world batches and many small model/particle draws. Correctness, buffer lifetime, and state churn must be visible before optimization.
scope: Inventory vertex attributes used by the selected BSP, alias, skeletal, sprite, and particle paths.
Define Xbox vertex formats and conversion rules.
Implement static and transient vertex/index buffer allocation.
Implement indexed/non-indexed triangles and required primitive modes.
Add state caching that avoids redundant NV2A commands without hiding state bugs.
Split oversized batches deterministically.
Count draw calls, triangles, vertices, state changes, bytes uploaded, and transient-buffer wraps.
Add debug validation for index bounds, stride, alignment, and buffer lifetime.
acceptance: Known geometry patterns render with correct winding, depth, culling, and interpolation.
Static geometry is not re-uploaded every frame.
Oversized batches split with identical visual output.
Submission counters match independently calculated test content.
No transient buffer overwrite occurs under the combined stress profile.
evidence: CPU profile of submission path before and after state caching.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Implement Xbox texture formats, mipmaps, uploads, and eviction
issues.objective: Load and manage the selected world/model/UI textures within the 64 MB budget and NV2A format constraints.
issues.context: DarkPlaces texture code assumes GL objects and desktop-capable formats. Texture residency and conversion are central to the texture-heavy zones and are likely the largest controllable memory consumer.
scope: Inventory actual source formats and dimensions in the selected content set.
Define accepted runtime formats, swizzle/layout rules, mip policy, alpha handling, cubemap handling, and fallback conversion.
Decide which conversion happens offline versus at runtime.
Implement create/upload/bind/update/destroy and texture identity tracking.
Implement deterministic residency/eviction with pinning for critical UI/lightmaps.
Measure conversion time, upload bytes, hit/miss/eviction counts, and resident memory.
Provide missing/unsupported texture placeholders with a clear diagnostic.
acceptance: Diffuse, alpha-tested, lightmap, normal/DOT3 candidate, cubemap candidate, and UI textures render correctly or use the documented fallback.
A texture-pressure scenario stays inside the configured cap and evicts deterministically.
Mip selection avoids obvious corruption and is reproducible between xemu and hardware.
Repeated scene loops do not leak texture allocations.
evidence: Format support table populated with tested assets.
Texture residency timeline for the texture-heavy zone.
Reference captures from xemu and hardware.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Render the console, menus, fonts, loading screen, and telemetry overlay
issues.objective: Make the port operable and diagnosable without relying on an external debugger.
issues.context: The console and overlay are required long before full 3D compatibility. They also exercise texture upload, alpha blending, orthographic transforms, and small batched draws.
scope: Render solid/colorized quads, textured quads, text glyphs, and scissor regions.
Support the DarkPlaces console and minimum menu/loading UI.
Create a low-allocation benchmark overlay showing workload marker, frame/time statistics, memory, draw/triangle counts, and warning state.
Make overlay sampling frequency configurable so measurement overhead can be quantified.
Provide a safe early-error screen that does not depend on the full material system.
acceptance: Console text remains legible on the baseline video mode and overscan-safe area.
Menus accept controller input.
Overlay values match logged values at sampled checkpoints.
Disabling the overlay removes its measurable draw/CPU cost.
Fatal startup messages remain visible even if 3D initialization fails.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Render Quake 3 BSP visibility, world geometry, and lightmaps
issues.objective: Render the selected Nexuiz world format with normal DarkPlaces visibility and world batching.
issues.context: Nexuiz 2.5.2 content primarily relies on Quake 3 BSP-derived maps and shader/material metadata. This is the first milestone that turns the backend into a useful world renderer.
scope: Confirm the exact BSP/version/features used by candidate maps.
Load BSP surfaces, nodes/leaves, visibility data, lightmaps, and relevant entities.
Preserve PVS/frustum culling and measure visible versus submitted surfaces.
Build reusable Xbox world buffers and lightmap resources.
Render opaque lightmapped world surfaces with depth/culling correctness.
Support sky masking/basic sky according to the feature matrix.
Add debug views for clusters, surfaces, lightmaps, overdraw proxy, and culled/submitted counts.
acceptance: A candidate map loads and renders navigable world geometry with lightmaps.
PVS/frustum changes visibly and numerically reduce submissions.
World buffers remain resident without per-frame rebuild.
xemu and hardware captures agree within documented raster differences.
Malformed/unsupported BSP features fail with map and lump context.
evidence: Reference camera captures and surface/triangle counters.
Memory breakdown for BSP, collision, lightmaps, and world buffers.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Render required model formats and animation paths
issues.objective: Support the animated entities needed to make the stress world representative rather than a static map flythrough.
issues.context: DarkPlaces supports multiple alias and skeletal model formats and both CPU/GPU animation paths. The Xbox build should implement only the formats actually selected for the benchmark and must avoid uncontrolled temporary buffers.
scope: Inventory model formats, skin counts, bone counts, vertex counts, and animation modes used by candidate content.
Choose CPU skinning/interpolation first unless a measured GPU path is justified.
Implement required alias/skeletal vertex generation and Xbox buffer upload/update.
Support model skins, fullbright/glow masks where selected, frame interpolation, transforms, and culling.
Cap bones/vertices and report unsupported assets at load time.
Measure animation CPU time and dynamic-buffer bytes.
acceptance: Every benchmark-required model format has a tested sample.
Animation is stable and synchronized across repeated runs.
Model memory and transient updates stay inside their caps.
Unsupported formats or limits fail before the benchmark starts.
Reference poses match desktop DarkPlaces closely enough for the workload purpose.
evidence: Desktop versus Xbox reference captures at named animation frames.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Translate materials into bounded NV2A state and multipass recipes
issues.objective: Map the benchmark's actual material combinations to deterministic NV2A recipes instead of attempting arbitrary GLSL permutation parity.
issues.context: DarkPlaces currently compiles many GLSL modes and permutations for diffuse/specular/fog/glow/reflection/water/shadow and other effects. NV2A requires a constrained set of vertex-program/register-combiner/multipass recipes.
scope: Collect all material flags and shader stages used by candidate benchmark assets.
Normalize them into a finite Xbox material key.
Implement recipes for opaque lightmapped, vertex-lit, alpha-tested, alpha-blended, additive, multitexture, fogged, glow/emissive, and selected environment-mapped surfaces.
Define pass ordering, depth-write, blend, alpha-test, cull, and texture-stage behavior.
Implement a visible fallback material keyed by unsupported reason.
Cache recipes and count recipe switches/passes.
Document visual approximations and workload impact versus desktop.
acceptance: Every selected benchmark material resolves to a named recipe or a preapproved fallback.
Unknown combinations never silently select an unrelated recipe.
Recipe switching and multipass counts are exposed in telemetry.
Alpha/depth ordering remains stable through the full camera path.
No runtime GLSL compiler dependency remains in the Xbox target.
evidence: Generated material coverage report for benchmark content.
Unsupported/fallback report with zero unexpected entries at release gate.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Port particles, sprites, decals, transparency sorting, and overdraw-heavy effects
issues.objective: Render the particle- and alpha-heavy zones with controlled batching and predictable overdraw.
issues.context: Particles and layered alpha effects are required stress content, but naïve one-draw-per-particle submission or per-frame allocation would test port inefficiency more than the intended hardware/emulator paths.
scope: Support required billboard, beam/trail, sprite, decal, additive, and alpha-blended forms.
Batch compatible effects into transient buffers.
Preserve deterministic simulation seed/order and document any visual sorting approximation.
Implement bounded transparency sorting without unbounded temporary allocation.
Expose particles, quads, batches, sort count/time, and estimated layer/overdraw indicators.
Add configurable load scaling for the stress profile.
acceptance: Selected particle and sprite effects render through all camera angles without persistent corruption.
Load scaling changes particle count predictably.
Submission cost grows sublinearly compared with one draw per particle.
Particle buffers and sort storage remain bounded over a one-hour loop.
Repeated runs produce matching particle workload counters.
evidence: CPU profile and draw-call comparison before/after batching.

issues.title: [Phase 2] Implement dynamic lighting, DOT3/normal mapping, reflections, fog, and effect fallbacks
issues.objective: Add the expensive visual workloads needed by the mixed scene while keeping each effect bounded and classifiable.
issues.context: The benchmark needs math- and fill-heavy regions, but modern DarkPlaces effects such as deferred lighting, shadow maps, relief mapping, and arbitrary shader permutations exceed a practical first NV2A target.
scope: Implement a bounded dynamic-light path with explicit maximum visible lights and passes.
Implement selected DOT3/normal-map lighting using supported NV2A texture/combiner behavior.
Implement selected cubemap/environment reflection and fog recipes.
Define water/refraction, realtime shadow, bloom/HDR, relief/offset mapping, and deferred-lighting fallbacks.
Provide per-effect enable/scaling controls and telemetry.
Prevent one unsupported effect from disabling unrelated material features.
Measure fill, passes, state changes, and memory impact by workload zone.
acceptance: The lighting/math zone exercises a documented NV2A vertex/combiner workload.
Effect limits are enforced and reported rather than overflowing buffers or time budgets.
Every deferred/disabled effect has a visible/documented fallback.
Combined-zone behavior is stable for one hour on retail memory.
Per-effect counters identify which workload is active.
evidence: Feature matrix updated with tested status.
Reference captures and timing/counter table per effect.

issues.title: [Phase 3] Audit Nexuiz 2.5.2 content and select a redistributable benchmark subset
issues.objective: Choose the exact maps, textures, models, sounds, scripts, and gamecode that may be modified and redistributed with the benchmark.
issues.context: The Nexuiz release combines engine, gamecode, and many assets. GPL engine/gamecode status does not automatically prove that every individual media file has a compatible license or source.
scope: Inventory candidate maps and every transitively referenced asset.
Record author, source location, license, required attribution, editable source availability, and redistribution status.
Exclude any asset with unknown, noncommercial-only, proprietary, or incompatible terms.
Prefer source assets and map sources that permit modification.
Record the original file hash and every transformation applied.
Define whether the repository stores source assets, generated Xbox assets, or only a reproducible acquisition manifest.
Review names/logos/trademarks separately from code licensing.
acceptance: Every shipped byte has a recorded source and redistribution basis.
The selected subset can be rebuilt without copying files from an installed proprietary game.
Excluded/uncertain assets are named and cannot enter release artifacts through wildcard packaging.
Attributions and source-offer obligations are documented.
evidence: Machine-readable content manifest with hashes and license identifiers.
Artifact scan proving no unmanifested media is packaged.

issues.title: [Phase 3] Build a host-side Xbox asset preparation and cache pipeline
issues.objective: Move expensive, deterministic conversion out of the 64 MB runtime while preserving traceability to source assets.
issues.context: Texture swizzling, mip generation, resampling, model packing, material-key generation, and content validation should not be repeated at Xbox startup when they can be verified offline.
scope: Define a versioned generated-asset format and cache key including tool version, source hash, settings, and target format.
Convert/validate textures, mip chains, cubemaps, lightmaps, models, vertex/index data, and material recipes needed by the selected content.
Reject unsupported dimensions, formats, shader stages, model limits, and memory estimates before packaging.
Generate a package manifest with source-to-output mapping and expected runtime memory.
Make outputs reproducible and stable across clean runs.
Keep tools cross-platform and free of proprietary SDK dependencies.
Decide which generated files are committed versus produced in CI/release jobs.
acceptance: Two clean conversions produce byte-identical outputs and manifest.
The runtime can load converted data without redoing host-only work.
Conversion failure identifies the source asset and violated limit.
Predicted runtime memory is within an agreed tolerance of measured residency.
Only manifest-approved assets enter the XISO.
evidence: Reproducibility hashes from two clean runs.

issues.title: [Phase 3] Implement the deterministic camera path and continuous loop controller
issues.objective: Drive one uninterrupted, repeatable flythrough that exposes the same visible workload sequence on every run.
issues.context: The target is not a menu of microtests. A slowly moving camera must cross connected areas while workload markers allow profiles and logs to correlate behavior with content.
scope: Choose recorded demo playback, QuakeC-controlled camera splines, or a hybrid and document the reason.
Use time- or distance-parameterized paths with deterministic interpolation and look direction.
Define named workload markers and warm-up/cool-down boundaries.
Loop without reinitializing the engine unless an explicit restart profile is selected.
Handle pause, resume, skip-to-marker, restart, and missed-frame recovery without changing event order.
Hash camera state and marker transitions.
Provide a path-authoring/export workflow that does not require editing binary data.
acceptance: Three runs enter every marker at the same simulation tick and camera transform within tolerance.
Loop transition is visually continuous or intentionally masked and does not leak memory.
Pause/resume and temporary frame delay do not reorder workload events.
The path completes in both xemu and retail hardware.
evidence: Marker timeline and camera-state hashes for repeated runs.
Loop-boundary memory and timing comparison across ten loops.

issues.title: [Phase 3] Author the connected mixed-workload stress world and scaling profiles
issues.objective: Create the large continuous world that transitions through representative geometry, texture, alpha/fur, particle, math, animation, lighting, combined, and recovery workloads.
issues.context: The project exists to expose mixed emulator/hardware bottlenecks over time. Each zone must be visually connected, measurable, and intentionally stressful without degenerating into an accidental malformed workload.
scope: Lay out connected zones for baseline, large vista/geometry, texture residency and switching, alpha vegetation/shell fur, particles/overdraw, deform/math, animated entities, dynamic lighting/effects, combined peak, and recovery.
Define low, standard, high, and torture profiles by data-driven multipliers or content groups.
Make transitions gradual enough to observe rising/falling subsystem load.
Ensure each zone has a marker, target counters, expected active features, and memory expectation.
Avoid occluding all expensive work merely to inflate nominal object counts.
Include repeated motifs only where they test a named behavior.
Keep the standard profile inside retail memory; high/torture may reduce quality or fail early according to documented limits.
acceptance: One complete path exercises every required workload class without returning to a scene-selection menu.
Zone counters prove the intended workload is visible/submitted.
Standard profile loops for one hour on 64 MB hardware.
Profiles change load monotonically for their declared dimensions.
Recovery zone returns counters and memory near the documented steady baseline.
evidence: Full-loop video plus xemu and hardware result files.

issues.title: [Phase 3] Implement benchmark telemetry, workload markers, and result files
issues.objective: Produce machine-readable measurements that distinguish simulation, renderer submission, GPU wait/present, content load, and memory behavior over the continuous world.
issues.context: Average FPS alone hides frame pacing, capped presentation, workload transitions, and regressions that only occur in specific zones.
scope: Define a versioned result schema containing build/content/profile identity.

Record frame time distribution, simulation time, render preparation/submission time, waits/present, draw/triangle/vertex counts, texture upload/residency/eviction, particles, lights/passes, memory current/peak, and workload marker.
Record average, median, p90, p95, p99, worst, and sample count per marker and full loop.
Separate warm-up and invalid/recovery frames from accepted samples.
Include dropped/late frames and timer-resolution metadata.
Write append-safe result files and a compact completion summary.
Measure telemetry overhead and support a reduced mode.
acceptance: The same result schema parses on the host without log scraping.
Every accepted frame belongs to exactly one marker/loop/profile.
Statistics recomputed from raw frame samples match the embedded summary.
Interrupted runs are marked incomplete rather than reported as valid.
Telemetry overhead is quantified and stays within the accepted threshold.
evidence: Schema document and sample result files.

issues.title: [Phase 3] Create a desktop reference mode for content and path validation
issues.objective: Run the same selected content, camera markers, and profile definitions on desktop DarkPlaces as a behavioral and authoring reference.
issues.context: The Xbox renderer will intentionally approximate some visuals. A desktop reference is still valuable for camera timing, asset completeness, workload activation, and spotting port-specific omissions.
scope: Add a benchmark launch configuration for the existing SDL build.
Use the same content manifest, camera path, profile names, marker IDs, and deterministic seeds.
Emit the same identity and state-hash fields even when graphics counters differ.
Capture reference images at fixed marker/checkpoint frames.
Define which visual differences are expected and which indicate missing content or sequencing.
acceptance: Desktop and Xbox runs traverse identical marker/tick sequences.
All selected assets load in the desktop reference with no unexpected fallback.
Reference captures are reproducible from documented commands.
The desktop benchmark path does not alter ordinary DarkPlaces behavior unless explicitly selected.
evidence: Desktop result file and marker/state hash comparison.

issues.title: [Phase 4] Automate xemu launch, result extraction, validation, and artifact packaging
issues.objective: Turn the benchmark into a repeatable xemu workload that can validate port changes and xemu performance branches without manual interaction.
issues.context: The stress world is intended to help xemu development. The host harness must launch a known build/profile, detect completion or failure, retrieve results, and preserve evidence with exact identities.
scope: Define a supported xemu invocation and isolated test-data directory.
Stage XBE/XISO/content without depending on a developer's existing Xbox files.
Select profile/loop count through a deterministic configuration or launch file.
Detect boot, marker progress, successful completion, fatal error, timeout, and emulator crash.
Retrieve result/log files and compute hashes.
Validate schema, build/content identity, loop completeness, state hashes, and required markers.
Package binary, configuration, raw results, summary, logs, xemu commit/config, host information, and screenshots/captures where requested.
Return nonzero on invalid/incomplete runs.
acceptance: One command executes a standard xemu run from a clean staged directory.
Success, timeout, engine fatal, and emulator crash are distinguished.
The harness rejects stale or mismatched result files.
The evidence package is self-describing and reproducible.
No retail BIOS, EEPROM, keys, or copyrighted content is committed or uploaded.
evidence: Sample successful and intentionally failed evidence packages.

issues.title: [Phase 4] Add fixed-checkpoint visual and counter validation
issues.objective: Detect rendering regressions that do not crash the engine or significantly change aggregate timing.
issues.context: A native NV2A backend can produce missing passes, stale textures, incorrect blend/depth state, or animation corruption while still completing the loop.
scope: Choose fixed simulation ticks at representative markers.
Capture framebuffer images or the best supported deterministic screen evidence.
Compare xemu captures against approved Xbox-renderer references using tolerant metrics and targeted masks where raster differences are expected.
Compare scene counters, material recipe coverage, fallback count, and state hashes at the same checkpoints.
Store approved references with build/content identity and review history.
Require human review for large visual-reference changes.
acceptance: A deliberately omitted texture/pass is detected.
Small expected raster differences do not create constant false failures.
No unexpected fallback material is present at release checkpoints.
Counter and state mismatches identify the marker and expected/actual values.

issues.title: [Phase 4] Validate and soak the standard profile on retail 64 MB hardware
issues.objective: Prove the standard benchmark is stable on the actual baseline console rather than only in xemu or on upgraded hardware.
issues.context: xemu can differ in timing, allocation tolerance, filesystem behavior, audio buffering, and NV2A corner cases. Retail-memory hardware is the acceptance authority for resource limits.
scope: Define a hardware test matrix covering at least the available console revisions/video paths and launch methods.
Run boot, one-loop, ten-loop, one-hour, and extended overnight soak cases.
Record crashes, hangs, visual corruption, audio underruns, memory high-water, temperature if available, and loop timing.
Test cold boot, warm restart, controller reconnect, writable storage unavailable/full, and interrupted result write.
Compare marker sequence and accepted state hashes with xemu.
Repeat after every renderer/memory change classified as high risk.
acceptance: The standard profile completes one hour on a 64 MB retail console without crash, GPU hang, corruption, unbounded memory growth, or invalid result.
Loop-to-loop memory returns within the documented tolerance.
Known hardware-specific differences are recorded and do not invalidate workload sequencing.
128 MB results are clearly separated and never used to pass the baseline gate.
evidence: Hardware matrix and console revision details that are safe to publish.
Raw logs/results for all acceptance runs.

issues.title: [Phase 4] Profile and tune the standard workload without weakening its coverage
issues.objective: Remove accidental port overhead and establish stable benchmark headroom while preserving the intended workload classes.
issues.context: The first working port will likely contain avoidable uploads, state churn, conversions, synchronization, cache misses, or allocations. Optimizing by deleting the stressful content would defeat the benchmark.
scope: Collect per-marker CPU profiles/counters for simulation, culling, material preparation, draw submission, texture work, animation, particles, audio, and waits.
Identify redundant state changes, uploads, synchronization, allocations, and conversions.
Make one hypothesis-driven change per measurement series.
Compare xemu and hardware to distinguish emulator-specific from port-specific hot paths.
Track visual/state/counter equivalence and memory after every optimization.
Document deliberate workload changes separately from engine optimizations.
Set accepted performance/headroom ranges without converting the suite into a pass/fail FPS contest.
acceptance: No accepted optimization removes a required zone or silently lowers the standard profile.
Every merged optimization includes before/after raw evidence and regression checks.
Frame-time distribution, memory, and counters remain interpretable per marker.
The final standard workload has enough headroom to complete reliably while retaining peak stress zones.
evidence: Final per-marker performance/counter table on xemu and hardware.
List of remaining known bottlenecks and whether they are port, hardware, or emulator concerns.

issues.title: [Phase 4] Produce the redistributable release package and document known limits
issues.objective: Publish a clean, reproducible benchmark package with source, license compliance, usage instructions, and complete limitation disclosures.
issues.context: A technically working XBE is not releasable until content provenance, GPL obligations, build reproducibility, excluded proprietary files, and expected renderer approximations are clear.
scope: Generate source and binary release manifests with SHA-256 hashes.
Package only manifest-approved content and generated assets.
Include GPL license text, source correspondence/build instructions, third-party notices, authorship/attribution, and nxdk references.
Document installation and launch for xemu and real hardware without distributing BIOS/EEPROM/keys.
Document supported modes/profiles, memory baseline, renderer fallbacks, unsupported effects, known bugs, result schema, and evidence interpretation.
Run secret/proprietary/binary allowlist scans.
Tag the exact source and content/tool versions used.
acceptance: A clean environment can rebuild the release from documented sources and pinned versions.
Binary and source manifests match the published artifacts.
No unmanifested or prohibited file is present.
The standard profile has current xemu and retail-hardware acceptance evidence.
Known limitations are linked from the release notes rather than hidden in issues.
